title: Top 5 Games that Deserved More Attention
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OddgScxecfA

Daniel (@dungeondive) picks five games the hobby underserved, and for each one argues both halves of the case: why it was overlooked, and why it shouldn't have been. A theme emerges almost immediately — most of these were sunk by how they looked rather than how they played, and nearly all of them are now dead.

*Champions of Hara* is bright and colourful enough to read as a light family game, which misdirects the audience that would actually love it: Tom Chick called it a better *Mage Knight*, and Daniel agrees. *Space Cadets: Away Missions* has the opposite problem — a grey, inert table presence hiding one of his favourite dice systems, where surplus successes become a currency you spend on interesting things. *Hand of Fate: Ordeals* was strangled by Kickstarter exclusives and a licence that will keep it out of print; he wants someone to lift the engine into a new setting, because it is still the best deck-building adventure game he knows.

*Darkest Night* second edition suffers from a one-action turn that sounds crippling and is in fact the point — guerrilla warfare in small increments, with some thirty-seven characters. And at number one, *Myth*: a catastrophic rulebook, a legendary Kickstarter failure, an edition upgrade maze, and beneath all of it a genuinely unique modular skirmish sandbox. "The best game I wouldn't wish upon my worst enemy."

----

Which underappreciated game would you most like to see rescued — reprinted, reimplemented, or simply rediscovered?
